Date: 2026-10-01T20:22:00Z
Subject: Production degradation impacting throughput — urgent

Hi Karthik,

We started seeing a sharp degradation in the Redwood-backed inference tiers for Helios at ~16:10 PT today. 95th p latency jumped from ~220ms to >1s for multi-token chat requests, error rate on our critical /v1/generate endpoint climbed to 6.4% (was <0.5%), and overall throughput dropped by ~45% across our busiest routes. This is causing timeouts in two customer-facing features and multiple support tickets.

I attached a small bundle of request traces and API logs (api-logs-20261001.zip) — the traces show repeated retry patterns and sustained 5xx spikes. We need an urgent remediation plan and clarity on commercial remedies under the SLA (credits/refund). Our procurement and legal teams are watching this closely.

As next steps we need:
- An exec-level point of contact for Helios while you investigate
- A short remediation timeline (hours -> days)
- An initial estimate of any credit/redress you’ll provision pending root-cause confirmation

Can you confirm receipt and propose a 30–45m exec-ops call today or tomorrow morning PT?

Thanks,
Laura Chen
Director of Platform Engineering
Helios Systems

Attachments: api-logs-20261001.zip (log bundle, 2.3MB)

Laura — thanks for the quick heads-up and the logs. I’ve looped in Marissa (sales lead), Vivek (head of customer success), and Monica from Ops so we can coordinate a live remediation and the commercial response. We’ve received the bundle and will start a focused triage immediately.

Immediate plan (first 3 hours):
- Ops: collect extended traces and confirm whether this is a serving runtime regression vs. routing/capacity mismatch (Monica)
- Mitigation: temporarily route sensitive routes to a higher-throughput pool and enable aggressive prefix caching for chat sessions to blunt the latency spike (we can flip this in ~15–45m)
- Communications: we’ll run hourly status updates until mitigated; I’ll be the exec POC for Helios for this incident (karthik@redwood.com)

Commercial stance: we are prepared to provision provisional credits while we complete the RCA. Marissa will propose a credit framework that aligns with your contract. We’ll commit to a formal remediation offer once we have the incident timeline validated.

Suggested windows for the exec-ops call: 2026-10-01 23:00Z / 2026-10-02 00:00Z / 2026-10-02 15:00Z (PT morning). Please confirm which works for your team.

-Karthik
VP, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Laura — following the triage call, thanks for the clear reproducer and for being candid about impact. Per our discussion, here is the provisional commercial pathway we’ll offer while we complete the post-incident RCA and a formal SLA credit calculation: 

1) Provisional credit: a rolling credit equal to 100% of your per-token invoice for the impacted routes during the incident window (2026-10-01T16:05 PT -> 2026-10-01T19:40 PT), applied as account credit within 5 business days. Final amount to be reconciled after RCA.

2) Service remediation: immediate routing changes and a targeted config patch that reduced error rate to ~0.6% in our canary; full rollout scheduled within 12 hours. Ops has preserved CVs and trace bundles (we listed files to the shared drive).

3) Contract amendment path: if the final RCA identifies a Redwood platform regression, we’ll propose a one-time commercial remedy (credit or fee waiver) and an SLA clarification addendum. We’ll share a draft amendment (redwood_sla_memo_v1.docx) for your legal review by end of day tomorrow.

4) Exec review: schedule a 45m call with our COO and your procurement/legal team to sign off on the remediation and the credit calculation.

Please confirm acceptance of the provisional credit approach so we can lock it in and route it to Finance. If you prefer a fixed-dollar offer instead of a usage credit, we can provide that option in the draft amendment.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Director, Customer Success (Commercial)
